$comment: Values emitted from docs/design/design-system.manifest.json that no component reads. `scripts/verify-token-reach.mjs` fails on any emitted name that is neither read nor listed here, AND on any name listed here that a component does read — both directions, because a dead exemption is how a live one gets waved through later. Every entry carries a `why` and a `cites`, and the whole list PRINTS ON EVERY RUN rather than only on a failure: an exemption nobody reads is an exemption nobody weighs. Same shape as retired-surface.json. See F-092 and .harness/plans/F-092-a-token-that-reaches-no-pixel.md.
$groupComment: `group` is required because `xs` is a radius step AND a type step, and they are not the same decision. One of them is read by 22 `size="xs"` literals; the other is read by nothing.
$readingComment: This file is a readable inventory of what the design system has DRAWN and the product has not yet BUILT. If it grows without anyone reading it, the citations are what makes that visible — an entry nobody can justify shows up as an entry with a weak one.

unreached.why: The web target. apps/mobile is the only surface (ADR-0051), so nothing in the reader zone imports these — their only reader is emit.test.ts, which is precisely the case this check reports. They are emitted anyway because four targets from one manifest is what stops web and mobile drifting the day a web surface exists (ADR-0020). Deleting them would remove the guarantee, not the dead code.

Emitted to CONSTRAIN, not to paint. TEXT_TOKENS is read only through its derived `TextToken` type, which is what stops `foreground.3` compiling below the large-text floor in Text.tsx. The other three are read in real code only by packages/ui/src/testing/conformance.ts, which this check deliberately does not count as a reader — that exclusion is what makes acceptance criterion 2 mean anything. A value whose job is to be checked against is a real value with no pixel, and that difference belongs here where it can be read rather than inferred.

Nothing in the product animates. There is no Animated, no withTiming and no transition anywhere in the reader zone — the durations and easings exist so that when something does move, the values are already decided rather than invented at the call site. The rule they belong to (motion may not animate a colour) is enforced from the manifest side by verify-motion.mjs, so it is guarded whether or not this binding is imported.

Every component that draws a line reaches for `border.strong` instead — the boundary of an outlined control, which is the case the components actually have. `border` is the translucent decorative hairline, and no surface built so far wants one. The four `.on.*` forms are the pre-composited values the contrast gate measured, never something a component reads: a component reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite it.

A scrim needs something to sit behind, and there is no dialog, bottom sheet or modal anywhere in the app yet — every screen in apps/mobile/src/screens is a full route. The first flow that needs one is the guided profile setup (F-026), and add-garment (F-043) after it. Same composite story as `border`: the `.on.*` forms are what the contrast gate measured, not what a component reads.

There is no chart in the product. The five-step near-achromatic ramp exists because a data series must be distinguishable without hue (golden rule 13), and deciding that under deadline is how a rainbow palette gets shipped. Wardrobe coverage and gap analysis (F-048) is the first surface that plots anything; the professional dE tables (F-055) are the second.

The token that exists to be restricted, and nothing paints it. Its usage is `largeText` — it fails AA against every surface below the WCAG large-text floor — so Text's `ColorFor<S>` type admits it only at a display or title size. The type permits it; no caller asks for it, and the one place a reader might expect it (the Home micro-label) carries a comment saying that label uses `foreground.2` and NOT this. Found only when this check stopped counting comments as reads: every mention of it in the reader zone is prose about why it is dangerous.

Steps of a scale that IS used — `sm`, `md`, `pill` and `swatch` are all read, so the scale itself is reaching components and only these three steps have found no surface. That is the ordinary state of a scale: some steps have found no surface yet. It is a different thing from a scale that reaches NOTHING while hand-written values contradict it — which is what `nativeSpacing` was until F-095, and why that entry was here and is now gone. The distinction is worth keeping written down, because it decides whether an entry is a note or a defect.

The 72px and 34px steps. The other five steps are read by 96 `size=` literals across the screens, so the scale reaches components — but no screen leads with a display size; every one of them opens at `title`. Neither is reached by nativeLargeTextSizes listing them either: a membership test is a question nobody answers with the token, which is why this check does not propagate through arrays. The editorial display type the design system was built around is, so far, not on any screen.

`Status` is built, conforms, and is rendered by no screen — it reaches gate 8's component half through the conformance registry, which ADR-0054 allows as a root, so nothing else reports it. All three kinds are handled by the component and none is requested by a caller. The first surface that shows one is outfit scoring and explainability (F-031). This entry exists so that a status channel nobody uses is a written-down fact rather than an assumption that it is used somewhere.
